feedback:
Written before this candidate has raced. It is iteration 9 (the best raced design, 98.24) with one change: geometry.wheel_track from 0.14 to 0.10 m. Everything else stays fixed (base_speed 0.9, kp 2.0, ki 0.4, kd 0.3, search_right, sensor y 0.05, x -0.07 to 0.07, sensor_size 0.016). The evidence behind it: iteration 9 widened the track from 0.12 to 0.14 m, and max_error stayed at the limit (oval 0.061, s-bend 0.0603, slalom 0.0623). Slalom progress fell from 0.113 to 0.101 and slalom line loss returned (0.6 events per trial). Iterations 0 to 9 have kept max_error pinned at 0.060 to 0.065 across gain, span, y, search-direction, and speed changes. The narrower track is the untested direction that should give more turn per wheel difference, which fits the slalom loss seen at 0.14. The candidate is valid and differs from the raced best by one field, so it is a clean test.

What to do after the race, depending on what it shows, judged against iteration 9 on max_error, line_loss_events and progress per track:
- If slalom line loss clears and slalom progress recovers toward or above 0.113, and max_error on oval or s-bend moves to 0.060 or below, keep wheel_track 0.10 and step base_speed up to 1.0 while checking that max_error stays under the limit.
- If max_error and progress are essentially unchanged, the drivetrain is not the lever. Then test sensor_size 0.012 at the wide span in the final iteration, and keep whichever of the 0.10 or 0.14 designs scored higher as the fallback.
- If slalom progress falls or line loss rises at 0.10, return to wheel_track 0.14 (the iteration 9 fallback) and do not vary the drivetrain further.
requested_changes: Keep iteration 9 unchanged except geometry.wheel_track = 0.10 (from 0.14). Slalom line loss returned at 0.14 (0.6 per trial) and slalom progress fell from 0.113 to 0.101, so the narrower track is the next test of turn authority.

If max_error drops to 0.060 or below on oval or s-bend and slalom line loss clears, keep wheel_track 0.10 and step controller.base_speed to 1.0 while checking that max_error does not rise above the limit.

If max_error stays at 0.061 or higher at both 0.14 and 0.10, the drivetrain is not the cause. Then set geometry.sensor_size = 0.012 at the wide span (x -0.07 to 0.07, y 0.05) as the final single-variable test, keeping the higher-scoring track width.
